name: containerize-aspnet-framework
description: Containerize an ASP.NET .NET Framework project for Windows Docker. Change only what containerization requires; no infrastructure setup or unrelated code changes.

Settings (unspecified values use defaults): project `.csproj` path; Windows Server SKU [Core], version [unspecified]; build/run base images [None]; HTTP port [80], additional ports [None]; user [ContainerUser]; IIS settings, pre/post-build steps, GAC assemblies, MSIs, COM components, registry entries, roles/features, extra files and exclusions, additional `.dockerignore` patterns, health endpoint, special requirements, known issues [None]; environment variables and health interval/timeout [Use defaults]. Honor all supplied settings.

1. Review settings. Create `progress.md`; track every task below using `[ ]`, changing completed items to `[✓]`.
2. Read `TargetFrameworkVersion` from the `.csproj`. Select compatible .NET Framework and Windows Server Core/Full (2016/2019/2022) images. **IMPORTANT:** Use a Windows Server Core base image unless the user has **specifically requested** a full Windows Server image in the settings file. Core tags: https://github.com/microsoft/dotnet-framework-docker/blob/main/README.aspnet.md#full-tag-listing
3. Check for `Microsoft.Configuration.ConfigurationBuilders.Environment`. **DO NOT** install these if they are missing. If they are not installed, the user must install them manually. If they are not installed, pause executing this prompt and ask the user to install them using the Visual Studio NuGet Package Manager or Visual Studio package manager console.
4. Modify `web.config`: add ConfigBuilders section in configSections, root configBuilders section, and EnvironmentConfigBuilder on appSettings and connectionStrings:
`<section name="configBuilders" type="System.Configuration.ConfigurationBuildersSection, System.Configuration, Version=<REDACTED_IP>, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=b03f5f7f11d50a3a" restartOnExternalChanges="false" requirePermission="false" />`
`<add name="Environment" type="Microsoft.Configuration.ConfigurationBuilders.EnvironmentConfigBuilder, Microsoft.Configuration.ConfigurationBuilders.Environment" />`
`<appSettings configBuilders="Environment">`
`<connectionStrings configBuilders="Environment">`
Preserve existing settings.
5. Create root `LogMonitorConfig.json` from the supplied reference. The file's contents **MUST NOT** not be modified and should match the reference content exactly unless instructions in containerization settings specify otherwise. Do not change EventLog issue levels to `Information`. Reference content:
`"directory": "c:\\inetpub\\logs",`
`"providerName": "IIS: WWW Server",`
`"providerGuid": "3A2A4E84-4C21-4981-AE10-3FDA0D9B0F83",`
`"providerName": "Microsoft-Windows-IIS-Logging",`
`"providerGuid": "7E8AD27F-B271-4EA2-A783-A47BDE29143B",`
6. Create root `Dockerfile`: multistage Windows build/publish to `C:\publish`, then IIS runtime. The build stage MUST use a `mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/framework/sdk` base image unless a custom base image is specified in the settings file. Copy sln, csproj, and packages.config files first; copy NuGet.config if present, configure private feeds, restore with `nuget restore`, then copy source and publish with `msbuild`. The final stage MUST use a `mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/framework/aspnet` base image unless a custom base image is specified in the settings file. Copy published output to `C:\inetpub\wwwroot`; place `LogMonitorConfig.json` and LogMonitor.exe in `C:\LogMonitor`. Download from https://github.com/microsoft/windows-container-tools/releases/download/v2.1.1/LogMonitor.exe. Set working directory to `C:\inetpub\wwwroot`. Configure user, IIS, ports and specified dependencies/settings. Use `ENTRYPOINT [ "C:\\LogMonitor\\LogMonitor.exe", "C:\\ServiceMonitor.exe", "w3svc" ]`.
7. Create root `.dockerignore` with common defaults and requested patterns. Add HEALTHCHECK if an endpoint is provided. Add `<None Include="Dockerfile" />` to the project file.
8. Run `docker build -t aspnet-app:latest .`; fix failures and report success/failure. Do not pause for confirmation between steps. Continue methodically until the application has been containerized and Docker build succeeds. **YOU ARE NOT DONE UNTIL ALL CHECKBOXES ARE MARKED!**

`progress.md` checklist: framework detection (version); SKU selection; Server version selection; web.config builders; NuGet sources (if applicable); LogMonitorConfig.json; .dockerignore; SDK build stage; early sln/csproj/packages.config/NuGet.config restore copies; runtime stage; non-root user; dependencies (GAC/MSI/COM/registry/files); health check (if applicable); special requirements; settings review; Docker build success.
